headline: A preprint reports workload-dependent savings from reversible agent context curation
summary: A 6 October arXiv preprint studies reversible, model-selected curation of tool results after they have been read: selected outputs are replaced with notes while exact originals remain recoverable. In one author-reported OpenTelemetry debugging-and-pivot pair, cumulative input tokens fall 50% and estimated API tariffs fall from USD 4.378–4.379 to USD 1.283–1.436, with both arms passing the same two-case primary oracle. The curated run takes 17% longer and uses more requests. A Planroom comparison shows no context or cost savings, and an earlier browser continuation has a lower manual quality score under curation. This is a narrow, exploratory and workload-dependent result; no independent reproduction or broad quality-preservation claim is established.
